INTRODUCTION.


This made-up introduction should be removed by the cleaner.




PARTS


The defence opens with a medium paragraph. It is long enough to stand on
its own as a single chunk, because it has more than forty words but
fewer than three hundred. It sets out the charges and promises to answer
each one of them in turn, plainly and without any rhetorical ornament.

Come here, Accuser, and answer a question. You care about the young?

Yes, I do.

Then tell the judges who improves them. You have taken great pains to
discover their corrupter, so you must know their improver as well.
Observe that you are silent and have nothing to say. Speak up, friend,
and tell us now who it is that improves them, for the judges are
waiting.

The laws.

But who, my friend, knows the laws?

The judges.

What, all of them, or only some of them and not the others?

All of them.

And the senators, do they improve the young as well?

Yes, the senators improve them.

After the exchange the speaker returns to a medium paragraph. It is
again long enough to stand alone, with more than forty words, and it
closes the cross-examination before the long speech begins below. It
adds one more sentence here so that it is clearly longer than forty
words in total.

Point 1 of the long speech is a plain sentence and then a few more words
to vary the length. Point 2 of the long speech is a plain sentence and
then a few more words to vary the length and then a few more words to
vary the length. Point 3 of the long speech is a plain sentence. Point 4
of the long speech is a plain sentence and then a few more words to vary
the length. Is point 5 of the long speech a question and then a few more
words to vary the length and then a few more words to vary the length?
Point 6 of the long speech is a plain sentence. Point 7 of the long
speech is a plain sentence and then a few more words to vary the length.
He said, “Point 8 of the long speech ends inside a quotation and then a
few more words to vary the length and then a few more words to vary the
length.” Point 9 of the long speech is a plain sentence. Point 10 of the
long speech is a plain sentence and then a few more words to vary the
length. Point 11 of the long speech is a plain sentence and then a few
more words to vary the length and then a few more words to vary the
length. Point 12 of the long speech is a plain sentence. Point 13 of the
long speech is a plain sentence and then a few more words to vary the
length. Point 14 of the long speech is a plain sentence and then a few
more words to vary the length and then a few more words to vary the
length. Is point 15 of the long speech a question? Point 16 of the long
speech is a plain sentence and then a few more words to vary the length.
Point 17 of the long speech is a plain sentence and then a few more
words to vary the length and then a few more words to vary the length.
He said, “Point 18 of the long speech ends inside a quotation.” Point 19
of the long speech is a plain sentence and then a few more words to vary

few more words to vary the length and then a few more words to vary the

the long speech a question and then a few more words to vary the length?
Point 26 of the long speech is a plain sentence and then a few more
words to vary the length and then a few more words to vary the length.
Point 27 of the long speech is a plain sentence. He said, “Point 28 of
the long speech ends inside a quotation and then a few more words to
vary the length.” Point 29 of the long speech is a plain sentence and
then a few more words to vary the length and then a few more words to
vary the length. Point 30 of the long speech is a plain sentence.


So he proposes death.

The penalty speech has one medium paragraph after a short opening line.
It weighs what the speaker deserves and proposes a fine instead, which
friends have offered to guarantee for him in court. It adds one more
sentence here so that it is clearly longer than forty words in total.


The final speech begins with a medium paragraph addressed to the judges
who condemned the speaker. It warns them that others will come after
him, and it speaks to his friends about death. It adds one more sentence
here so that it is clearly longer than forty words in total.

The hour of departure has arrived.
